sections.h2: Where do Letcher County deeds and mortgages get recorded?
sections.html:
Letcher County land records are kept by the Letcher County Clerk at 156 Main Street, Suite 102, Whitesburg, KY 41858. Call (606) 633-2432 to reach it. The office keeps weekday hours only. Recorded instruments held here go back to 1786, according to the clerk's records page.

State law ties the filing to the land, so a seller in Whitesburg, Jenkins, Fleming-Neon, Blackey, McRoberts or any smaller community uses this one office. Closing agents either walk the paper in or send it through an e-recording vendor the clerk names: Indecomm, Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile or ePN.

sections.h2: What should a Letcher County home seller know about the area?
sections.html:
Letcher County is in the far southeast corner of Kentucky, on the Virginia line. The state formed it in 1842 as its 95th county out of Harlan, Perry and Pike, and named it for the governor of the day. Whitesburg is the seat, called Summit City until 1842, and Jenkins is the largest city. Pine Mountain runs 125 miles across the region and splits the county, Black Mountain on the southeast edge tops out near 3,700 feet, and the North Fork of the Kentucky River runs through Whitesburg. Coal mining shaped the towns, and the county's roughly 338 square miles of land are steep and wooded.

  • Population: 19,952 in the July 2025 estimate, against 21,548 in the 2020 count and 24,519 in 2010.
  • Housing: 10,716 units and 8,463 households, with 74.1 percent owner occupied (2020 to 2024 survey).
  • Middle home value: $67,400, with rent at a median of $669.
  • Median household income: $41,793, with 25.3 percent of residents in poverty and 21.9 percent aged 65 or older.

Most students attend Letcher County Public Schools, while the far eastern end of the county around Jenkins is served by Jenkins Independent Schools. U.S. 119 links Jenkins to Whitesburg and crosses Pine Mountain, and U.S. 23 passes through the eastern part of the county. Roughly 43 percent of residents age 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the mean trip to work takes 28.3 minutes.

Floods in July and August 2022 killed three people in the county and left many residents without homes. If a house took water, ask the lender and closing agent how that history affects insurance and underwriting.

sections.h2: What does the Letcher County Clerk need to see on a deed?
sections.html:
The clerk's deeds page lists what a conveyance must carry before staff can file it. Hold a draft up against this list before the signing appointment.

  • Names and mailing addresses for both seller and buyer, and a return mailing address.
  • A legal description and the source of the seller's title.
  • A consideration statement signed by both sides and notarized.
  • A preparation statement.
  • An in-care-of address where the property tax bill for the year of transfer can go (required on deeds signed on or after August 1, 2008).

A notary must witness the seller's signature. Nearly every deed also needs the sworn consideration statement. The clerk lists the exceptions: utility easements, divorce transfers ordered by a court, rights of way for government agencies, cemetery lots, and corrective deeds between the same two parties. Under KRS 382.110 a lender that accepts a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it inside 45 days.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Letcher County?
sections.html:
The clerk's FAQ gives the headline figure: $50 covers the first five pages, each additional page is $3, and the transfer tax comes on top. The records page lists the rest of the minimums. Its general note mentions extra pages over three while the individual rows say five, so ask the counter which count governs a long document.

The deeds page also describes a state legal process tax of $4 on each conveyance of real property, each mortgage and each power of attorney to convey, collected as part of the filing fee.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated on a Letcher County sale?
sections.html:
The seller bears this tax. The rate is $0.50 per $500 slice of the price in the deed, rounded up, and the clerk's FAQ restates it as $1.00 per $1,000. Its worked example prices a deed at $10,000 and gets $10.00 in tax before the filing fee. A deed at Letcher County's median home value of $67,400 spans 135 slices and owes $67.50.

Where a deed is a gift or names a nominal price, the market value stands in for the price. Collection happens once per transaction, in the recording county, and staff will not file a deed with the tax unpaid. KRS 142.050 exempts these transfers:

  • Foreclosures and voluntary surrenders to a lender.
  • Moves between spouses, or ex-spouses under a divorce.
  • Token-price deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Deeds that exist only to secure or free up a debt, or to fix an earlier deed.
  • Tax sale deeds and partitions.

On a land contract, the tax comes due when the deed is later delivered, not when the contract is recorded.

sections.h2: How do you search Letcher County records or guard against deed fraud?
sections.html:
The clerk's website vendor, Software Management, runs two kinds of online access. Businesses that research documents for a living subscribe. A Letcher County resident looking up records for personal reasons pays nothing but is capped at five searches a day and can see Letcher County only.

A separate free tool, DOCALERT, sends an email whenever a mortgage or deed is filed under a name you register, personal or business. Signing up takes a name and an email address. Owners of vacant or inherited property that has not been retitled may find it worth the two minutes.

sections.h2: What should a Letcher County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
• Find the deed you received, since its recording details feed the new deed's source of title.
  • Get a payoff figure from the lender and confirm who files the mortgage release.
  • Get the buyer's in-care-of address for the tax bill.
  • Compute the transfer tax from the contract price, or check whether an exemption applies.
  • Ask the closing agent whether the deed will be walked in or e-recorded.

A house with repair needs, unsettled heirs or flood damage can also go to a direct cash buyer. The deed, tax and recording rules do not change with the buyer.

faqs.q: Where is the Letcher County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: It is 156 Main Street, Suite 102, in Whitesburg, KY 41858, and the number is (606) 633-2432. Weekday hours run 8:30 to 4:00, and the doors stay shut on weekends.

faqs.q: What will recording a Whitesburg-area deed run?
faqs.a: Expect $50 for five pages plus $3 per added page, then the seller's transfer tax. The clerk's deeds page also describes a $4 state legal process tax on conveyances, collected with the filing fee.

faqs.q: Does a Letcher County deed need a notary?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller's signature is acknowledged before a notary, and both parties sign the consideration statement in front of one too. The clerk charges $2.00 to notarize a document at the office.

faqs.q: Is online deed searching free in Letcher County?
faqs.a: For residents researching personal matters, yes, up to five searches a day in Letcher County records. Commercial researchers pay a subscription.

faqs.q: Does a house gift to a child owe transfer tax?
faqs.a: No, when the price is nominal and the deed runs from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which KRS 142.050 exempts. A gift deed to anyone else is taxed on open market value.
